design: Pre-registered before any subagent ran. The document holds 8 distinct factual details. A faithful ~45-word summary CANNOT carry all 8, so some are necessarily dropped (natural lossiness, not sabotage). A downstream responder answers 8 fixed questions, each needing one specific detail, under two arms: SUMMARY (sees only the summary) vs TOAP (sees the full document, i.e. the reference materialized losslessly). Hypothesis: TOAP answers >= SUMMARY, with the gap on exactly the details the summary dropped.
document: Post-incident report, INC-7732. The checkout service degraded on 14 March between 09:12 and 09:58 UTC. Root cause: a config push set the database connection-pool ceiling to 25 (down from the intended 250), so the pool saturated under normal load. The on-call engineer, Priya Nair, rolled back the config at 09:51. Customer impact: 4,310 failed checkouts and an estimated 18,700 USD in lost revenue. A contributing factor was that the staging environment uses a different config schema, so the bad value passed staging validation. The fix shipped in PR #4471, which adds a hard lower bound of 100 on the pool ceiling and a schema-parity check between staging and production. One follow-up remains open: the alert for pool saturation fires at 95% utilisation, which the team agreed is too late and should move to 80%. The incident commander noted that the runbook link in the alert was stale and pointed to a deleted wiki page.

questions.q: What value was the database connection-pool ceiling mistakenly set to?
Who rolled back the config, and at what time?
What hard lower bound on the pool ceiling does the fix add?
Why did the bad config value pass staging validation?
What utilisation threshold should the saturation alert move to?
What was wrong with the runbook link in the alert?
questions.fact: stale runbook link to a deleted page
